definitions.explanation: A state of having lost honor or reputation. Can function as a noun (a disgrace) or as a na-adjective (dishonorable, disgraceful).

examples.japanese: {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{記録|きろく}を{作|つく}ってしまった。
examples.english: I ended up setting a disgraceful record.

examples.japanese: {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{敗北|はいぼく}を{喫|きっ}した。
{家族|かぞく}に{不名誉|ふめいよ}をもたらすようなことはしたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to do anything that would bring disgrace upon my family.

notes:
{不名誉|ふめいよ} describes a loss of honor or reputation. Functions as both a na-adjective ({不名誉|ふめいよ}な) and a noun.

FORMS:
{不|ふ} (negative prefix) + {名誉|めいよ} (honor, prestige).

AS NA-ADJECTIVE:
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{記録|きろく}: disgraceful record
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{敗北|はいぼく}: humiliating defeat
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{称号|しょうごう}: dishonorable title
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{結果|けっか}: shameful result

AS NOUN:
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}を{被|こうむ}る: to suffer disgrace
- {不名誉|ふめいよ}をもたらす: to bring dishonor

SIMILAR WORDS:
{名誉|めいよ} (honor, prestige). Compare {名誉|めいよ}ある{賞|しょう} (prestigious award) vs. {不名誉|ふめいよ}な{記録|きろく} (disgraceful record).

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal. In casual speech, {恥|は}ずかしい (embarrassing) or {情|なさ}けない (pathetic) express similar sentiments.
